_note: Tables CREATEd by a migration that shared/schema.ts does not model. Registered, not dropped: several hold data, and dropping a production table is customer-data deletion — a founder-only hard stop (CLAUDE.md). Each entry must say WHY the ORM does not own it. This register may only SHRINK: a table leaves it by being modelled in schema.ts, or by a founder decision to drop it. Discovered 2026-08-23 by standing up a real Postgres and running the Fly release_command, which reported it could not create earnest_money_events' append-only trigger — and exited 0.

orphans.sessions: connect-pg-simple's express-session store. Owned by the session middleware, not the app: the ORM must not model it, and its shape is the library's to change.
orphans.users: Pre-Clerk identity table. Auth is Clerk-backed now; the row shape is not the app's to define. Reachable only through raw SQL in legacy paths.
orphans.password_reset_tokens: Belongs to the pre-Clerk auth flow above. Retained because it may hold rows; nothing reads it.
orphans.referrals: Referral programme tables from an earlier growth build. Referenced in server/ only by raw SQL, never through the ORM.
orphans.autonomous_decisions: Superseded by the decision-snapshot model in shared/decisions/. Two server references, both raw SQL reads of historical rows.
orphans.voice_calls: Voice-call capture from the telephony build. The live path writes call_transcripts, which IS modelled; these are the older rows.
orphans.voice_call_recordings: Sibling of voice_calls. No reader or writer anywhere in server/.
orphans.satellite_analysis: Imagery-analysis output from the parcel-intelligence build. One raw-SQL reference; no ORM model.
orphans.satellite_snapshots: Sibling of satellite_analysis. No reader or writer anywhere in server/.
orphans.lead_photos: Field-capture photos from an earlier mobile build. No reader or writer anywhere in server/.
orphans.push_subscriptions: Web-push endpoints. Nothing in server/ sends web push; the notification rails are email, SMS and in-app.
orphans.automation_executions: Execution log for a workflow engine superseded by the outbox + scheduler. No reader or writer.
orphans.model_versions: ML model registry from the scoring build. Superseded by shared/schema ML snapshot tables, which ARE modelled.
orphans.training_metrics: Sibling of model_versions. No reader or writer anywhere in server/.
orphans.tenant_event_streams: Per-tenant event stream from an earlier eventing design. Superseded by lifecycle_events, which IS modelled.
orphans.earnest_money_events: Append-only EMD event log, with an immutability trigger installed by migration 0239. No reader or writer in server/. This is the table whose trigger the release command reported it could not create against a schema-built database — the finding that produced this register. Money-custody adjacent: see the fee tables below.
orphans.fee_audit_log: Residue of a transaction-fee design. AcreOS taking a fee out of customer money movement is what the 2026-07-29 founder ruling forbids — customer money never moves on AcreOS's own account — so this table should stay unmodelled and unused. Registered so its existence is known, not so it is revived. DELETION CANDIDATE (founder decision 2026-08-24): approved for eventual deletion ONLY after proving (a) no reachable consumer, (b) no required historical or migration purpose, and (c) no live production data requiring preservation. (a) is established — zero readers or writers anywhere in server/. (b) and (c) are NOT: production state is unknown from this environment, and the ruling is explicit that unknown production state means keep as a candidate rather than delete blindly. Do not drop this table on the strength of (a) alone.
orphans.fee_payout_schedules: Same design as fee_audit_log, same ruling. No reader or writer. DELETION CANDIDATE (founder decision 2026-08-24): approved for eventual deletion ONLY after proving (a) no reachable consumer, (b) no required historical or migration purpose, and (c) no live production data requiring preservation. (a) is established — zero readers or writers anywhere in server/. (b) and (c) are NOT: production state is unknown from this environment, and the ruling is explicit that unknown production state means keep as a candidate rather than delete blindly. Do not drop this table on the strength of (a) alone.
orphans.transaction_fee_settlements: Same design as fee_audit_log, same ruling. No reader or writer. Three dead fee tables together are the clearest artefact in the database of the payments architecture the money-custody hard stop replaced. (a) is established — zero readers or writers anywhere in server/. (b) and (c) are NOT: production state is unknown from this environment, and the ruling is explicit that unknown production state means keep as a candidate rather than delete blindly. Do not drop this table on the strength of (a) alone.
orphans.agent_resource_quotas: OD-8 drop batch 1 (founder 'approve with evidence' ruling 2026-08-29). The ORM model was removed with its dead V-tower service; migration 0241 drops the table IF it holds zero rows at release time. This entry records the interim (and the populated-survivor case): the table may still exist in production, unmodelled, until the release log confirms the drop or the founder rules on its rows. Remove this entry when the deploy-log evidence shows it dropped.

_deletionCandidates: Founder decision 2026-08-24 covers the three transaction-fee tables above. The precondition AcreOS can satisfy locally is 'no reachable consumer', and it is satisfied. The two it cannot — historical/migration purpose, and live production rows — require production evidence this environment does not have. Recording that boundary is the point: the tables stay, labelled, until someone can answer the other two.
